claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 can be prepared as melt-spun ribbons.
Under slow cooling, Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes extensive primary crystallization and develops a complex crystalline microstructure.
Melt-spinning produces only partial amorphization of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Quenching the alloy against a cryogenically cooled copper substrate will suppress primary crystallization and increase amorphous retention.
Cryogenic substrate-assisted quenching will increase the thermal stability of the amorphous alloy.
An intermediate thermal-management layer will minimize thermal shock while preserving rapid heat extraction.
Maintaining the substrate near 77 K will produce solidification cooling rates above 10^6 K/s.
Rapid latent-heat extraction reduces residence time in the critical nucleation-temperature window.
Reducing residence time in the nucleation window reduces the formation of primary crystalline nuclei.
The proposed treatment will produce a uniformly amorphous bulk structure.
Rapid cooling freezes the atomic configuration before diffusion can enable primary crystallization.
Faster cooling increases undercooling in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Cryogenic substrate-assisted quenching will suppress phase separation.
Relative to conventionally cooled material, the treated alloy will retain a larger amorphous fraction.
The treated alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature during DSC reheating.
The treated alloy will show diminished or delayed crystallization exotherms.
Slow cooling on a conventional copper plate occurs at approximately 52 K/s.
Rapidly quenched melt-spun ribbons may retain localized primary crystallization.
Enhanced amorphous retention requires cooling rates above approximately 10^6 K/s.
Reheating must use conventional DSC scan rates to accurately represent crystallization behavior.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis characterizes melt-spinning as producing partial amorphization or possible localized primary crystallization, whereas the cited same-system records report that melt-spinning at 10^5–10^6 K/s produced an amorphous structure.
The mediator predicts a uniformly amorphous bulk structure, but the proposed decisive experiment tests ribbons; ribbon results cannot directly establish bulk glass formation or bulk uniformity.
